stories.event: Americans vote on Tuesday 3 November 2026 in midterm elections for all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats (Republicans hold the House 218–214 and the Senate 53–47). Democrats lead the generic congressional ballot by about 8.6 points on average and need a net gain of three House seats and four Senate seats; mid-decade redistricting has moved about six House seats toward Republicans on paper. Close Senate races in Ohio, Texas, Maine, Kansas and Alaska decide control of the Senate.

research.question: Direction and size of polling-average errors in recent Senate races in red-leaning states (2018-2024), and whether they were correlated; and can Georgia's Senate race go to a runoff?
research.finding: Georgia: this part is decisive. Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_election_in_Georgia, read 1 Nov 2026) lists only two general-election candidates, Ossoff (D) and Collins (R), and cites the AJC article 'Libertarians won't be on the ballot in Georgia'. A runoff (1 Dec) happens only if no one wins a majority. With two names on the ballot, a runoff would need an exact tie or a significant write-in vote. Polling errors (Wikipedia final aggregate vs result; Dem margin error, negative = Republican beat the polls): TX 2024: Cruz +4.0 avg vs +8.49 result (-4.5). OH 2024: Moreno +1.0 vs +3.62 (-2.6). TX 2020: Cornyn +5.2/+6.5 vs +9.6 (-3.1 to -4.4). ME 2020: Gideon +3.8 (270toWin) vs Collins +8.6 (-12.4). IA 2020: Ernst +0.4/+1.4 vs +6.6 (-5.2 to -6.2). NC 2020: Cunningham +2.6/+2.8 vs Tillis +1.75 (-4.4). NC 2022: Budd +5.1 avg vs +3.2 (+1.9, Democrats beat the polls). FL 2024: Scott beat the final 538 average by 7.8 (blog, Jul 2025). TX 2018: individual polls only, Cruz +3 to +9 vs +2.57 (O'Rourke beat the polls). 2022 overall: Breitbart (10 Nov 2022) says Democrats ran about 3 points better than RCP averages, including OH +1.4 and NC +2.6 toward Democrats. The Federalist (28 Oct 2026, Anderson) gives 2016-2024 average Senate errors: ME R+4.3, IA R+3.6, MI R+2.5, NC R+1.7, TX R+1.0, OH R+1.0, GA D+0.3, MN D+2.3, NH D+3.4. Newsweek (1 Oct 2026) gives 2024 presidential figures: TX Trump +7.4 avg vs ~+14, OH +7.7 vs ~+11, IA +4.7 vs +13. Historical: the 'State of the Polls 2019' article (goodreads repost) says Senate bias averages 0.1 points with no consistent direction from cycle to cycle. Pattern: in 2020 and 2024 (presidential years with Trump on the ballot), errors in these states were all in the same direction, toward Republicans, by 2.6-12 points. In 2018 and 2022 (midterms), errors in these states were small or toward Democrats. This is evidence of a correlated, cycle-specific error, not a fixed pro-Democratic bias. It does not show the direction in 2026.

research.question: How far has AMD's actual revenue exceeded the midpoint of its own guidance in the last 6-8 quarters?
